opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, owned by the Engineer role. Full-time employees may have up to write, and the role owns the system, so write is within policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes about E004 conflict on employment type: HR reports full-time Engineer (max write, role owns Source Code), while Security reports contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive valid policy. Under the contractor/basic-training interpretation, requested write exceeds the maximum of read, so the maximum is granted: read. This never exceeds the requested level.
